title: a signal during the TPM seal no longer destroys the only KEK (H-BK-1)

findings.claim: seal_keys.sh (tpm, no kek.json, plain keys): a SIGTERM, SIGHUP or Ctrl-C during keys init shredded the only KEK after the keys were wrapped under it; fixed: the credential is sealed and placed before any key is wrapped, nothing removes it, a signal exits, a re-run finishes
seal_keys.sh's kek.json-exists branch exits before the D-887 chown: a run stopped before the chown leaves root-owned key files that a re-run does not hand to the services' user
seal_keys.sh shamir: a stop between keys init and keys unseal leaves a re-run that cannot open the KEK by itself (the shares are on the media; nothing is lost)
